body:
Gael’s history follows two connected eras: the war for a land Death had devastated, and the keeping of what its people restored. Nienna helps open the road; Nuru and Huoth make survival possible; the company creates and protects living ground. Later damage to Hope demands another choice to rebuild. Responsibility passes to people and institutions who inherit the first expedition’s unfinished work.

Gael’s map communicates emptiness before it communicates settlement. The Citadel of Sorrow, Mage’s Ruin, Plains of Trial, Vysaeth’s Tomb, Tower of Gael, and Underwater Temple stand across a landscape marked by catastrophe. Against that scale, Hope is tiny and green: a physical argument that life has established a beachhead in a dead or brutal land.

Danger becomes remembered geography

On 19 September 2024, a failed group navigation effort carried travelers into a quarter-mile field of gas geysers and salt-preserved bones. Going around risked night travel; crossing meant accepting the toxic ground directly. When another journey returned near the same field on 20 October, Saray recognized it, the party debated safer routes, Adelia tried to collect the yellow material, and Scribonia studied the geothermal rhythm. The terrain had not reset between quests. Prior experience changed what the next party could attempt.

Discovery and Death’s victory · June 2024

Nienna’s expedition reached Gael only after acquiring a ship and crew, encountering an island-sized moving turtle, finding a seed of the Great Tree, and learning that Death’s dragons haunted the Void. Titan’s Watch was the last safe land under the Eye. Its ruined Titan statues, decayed cathedral, and lifeless terrain showed what happened when Death defeated a place. The exact earlier dates in that expedition remain unresolved.

Nienna also knew of a supposedly safer Void route that fed unwilling souls to its inhabitants. The account describes her testimony about one method—not that every historical crossing used it.

The war for Gael: the people who open the road

Nienna is a catalyst for the Gael expedition. Gartina explicitly credits her with buying the ship and freeing its crew, setting in motion the discoveries connected with Quake’s island-sized turtle sighting, the Great Tree seed and the hazardous passage toward Gael. Nienna’s initiative helps make a new chapter possible; Gartina, Adelia and Elenia later give its restoration different forms.

Dale, Quake, Saray, Olokun, Scribonia and the wider company make the expedition a community rather than the work of a few isolated heroes. Research, carrying, cooking, healing and remembering losses become ways of continuing together.

Nienna’s deaths and the cost of continuing

The Plains of Trial scene posted on 9 July 2024 records Nienna and Saray continuing their hunt after defeating a fire-and-ash bird. They choose to stand against approaching soul eaters and wraiths. Nienna places herself before Saray and urges her to flee if she falls. Nienna dies; Saray defeats the remaining enemies and returns her body to the Tower. Her subsequent self-blame remains her judgment of the encounter.

On 15 July, Saray obtains a diamond through an offering at Nuru’s altar. Elenia casts Raise Dead and Nienna awakens. This first death and recovery are distinct from her later voluntary sacrifice during the Hallowing of Hope on 6 September.

Her earlier retreat after Jiangshi’s loss also remains morally distinct. Gartina argues that returning would likely have created another unrecoverable death. Nienna’s later choice to protect someone does not prove that every withdrawal was cowardice. The Hallowing preserves the difference between imposing a price on another person and choosing to spend one’s own life so others can continue.

Read the Hallowing of Hope and Nienna’s last run →

Huoth: guidance made practical

Nuru’s shelter reaches the expedition through Huoth as well as the Tower’s defences. Huoth welcomes, warns, advises, interprets offerings and encourages people who do not yet believe themselves capable of being heroes. He introduces the Crucible’s lesson of cooperation and helps make divine aid part of practical survival.

His later identification as an angel of Nuru does not erase this caretaker’s work or make the adventurers’ knowledge complete. When his physical watch ends in March 2025, the community must inherit the responsibility he helped sustain. Shelter and counsel support judgment; they do not guarantee that every rescue will succeed.

Hope: the first living ground

The early August 2024 description of Elenia and Adelia’s Hope names a patch of newly sanctified ground saved by their combined power and will. Nienna brings Gartina and Dale to see it and credits her friends. Gartina cries, removes her boots and rolls in the grass; Dale recognizes that the land may be saved and immediately considers how to protect the site.

The scene turns restoration from an idea into something the group can touch. It does not make the surrounding wilderness safe. The first living foothold still needs protection, materials and people willing to return. Adelia, Elenia and Nienna’s later sacrifice belong to a shared history; no single act completes it.

Stake and a forest: restoration becomes landscape

In the restoration scene recorded on 6 December 2024, Gartina organizes the spreading of crushed crustacean shells and limestone. Draygar has refined the limestone; Krone carries the heavy material; Scribonia helps transport and distribute it and brings gentle rain. Soil is mixed so the amendments will enter the ground. The work gives magical renewal a material foundation.

Gartina then plants her Staff of the Woodlands. The Writer describes it becoming a young Eastern White Pine. Krone suggests “steak,” and Gartina adopts Stake as a name for the group’s sacrifice, shared commitment and investment in reclaiming the land. The second tree begins with a joke and becomes a promise.

After mixing the soil, Gartina throws a magical seed into the area between Hope and Stake. The Writer describes a forest more than fifty miles across, with trees, animals, streams and ponds. Its scale belongs to that narrated account, rather than a newly surveyed map boundary. The forest later known as Shadow Angel Forest makes renewal visible across a landscape.

At the time, Gartina worries the seed may produce an illusion that will disappear. She hopes Hope, Stake and the Hallowing will help it endure; her hope is not a confirmed explanation of the magic. Later records treat the forest as a place that can be explored and inhabited. In August 2025, Sildithas credits Gartina’s staff and another magical item with bringing Stake and the forest into being. That later testimony supports continuity without proving every creature’s origin or permanent safety.

Fellowship before the battle

The Tower gives isolated explorers a home where meals, rest, grief, research and planning can continue. Homesickness for Pristinia does not vanish, but the people beside them increasingly become the community they can depend on.

Huoth’s introduction to the Crucible of Gael makes that dependence practical. Courage alone will not prepare them for Wrath. Teams must learn to support one another and adapt. Gael’s military preparation and its later restoration share the same requirement: different people must contribute different kinds of strength.

An older landscape beneath the campaign

Titan’s Watch stands just beyond the Tower as the last safe land under the Eye in its early description. Ruined Titan statues, a decayed cathedral and a river leading past the Tower to the sea mark a boundary between refuge and the island beyond. The Road leads toward the Plains of Trial and the interior, carrying travelers past abandoned monuments into unsafe territory. The Plains become a frontier of repeated expeditions, husk gathering and costly encounters.

Crustacean Cove is described as roughly two miles from the Tower, with a temple in an underwater cave beneath it. Its early description calls it safe; that does not guarantee every later expedition or settlement there. The source also uses the spelling Crustescean Cove.

Mage’s Ruin lies above the smog, in snow and strong wind. Its October 2024 description already identifies an active teleportation circle. The surviving record does not establish its original builders or make its active circle a consequence of Wrath’s later defeat.

In July 2025, Saray names the cathedral as a place where a God of Time was venerated and groups it with the sea temple, Mage’s Ruin, Vysaeth’s tomb and Wrath’s citadel as histories still needing investigation. Her account preserves a religious association, not the deity’s identity or a complete explanation of the cathedral’s mechanisms. The ruins are not all assigned to one civilization.

Vysaeth’s existing history already preserves his kingship, lichdom and interested testimony about Roderick. Those recovered facts remain alongside unanswered questions about his tomb and Gael’s wider past. Unfinished archaeology does not erase what is already known.

Liberation and early restoration · late 2024–2025

Gael was liberated from Wrath around late 2024, though fiendish stragglers remained on the Plains. Gartina’s statement—“Gael is free of Wrath’s taint. What was lost can begin to grow anew.”—defines the island’s present tense. It is wounded, but unlike a truly dead island, it can recover. Akarian is named as Guardian of Gael.

By February 24, 2025, Hope and Stake already existed, and Shadowangel Forest was new enough to require exploration. Gartina said she helped bring the changed terrain into existence. Adelia’s later 2026 transformation therefore expanded a restoration already underway; it did not begin life in an otherwise unchanged wasteland.

Refugees and settlement

Refugees arrived aboard a ship that crashed near Crustacean Cove. Around the Tower they lived mainly in huts and shacks, supplemented by occasional magical shelter. On February 24, 2025, Gartina and Dale moved from emergency care toward permanent planning: soup and conversation first, then a proposal to salvage the wreck for a longhouse, scout safer Plains for material, and—critically—ask the refugees what they wanted.

The problem did not vanish when life returned. Permanent infrastructure remained incomplete into 2026, and some people moved toward the developing frontier of Verdelune.

A developing society · 2026

By September 19, the Veilguard operated in Gael; husk hunts and a cult threat to one of Gael’s shards showed that danger persisted. The Ale-Chemy Knights had created an open-air market with areas for different skills, evidence of organized commerce in a region Marius remembered as having almost no economy. At least one trusted network could also transport known people safely to Gael from other islands—a striking contrast with the lethal Void journey of 2024, though the exact mechanism is unknown.

Thorn’s history preserves an unresolved causal chain: she died during a Gael husk hunt, her team left her body, a cult later attempted to use her in a shard-destruction ritual, and she was alive in Prima by September 2026. The archive does not yet establish how she returned or how the ritual ended.

A departure point for newer roads

By 7 September 2026, parties gathered on Gael’s coast for the many-hour journey through Verdelune toward Larkhollow. Gael had become familiar enough to serve as a staging ground while remaining unfinished in its own right: known routes and remembered hazards coexist with large regions that have never been meaningfully explored.

Trials, ruins, and testimony

Sildithas died in the Plains of Trial and was resurrected hours later, remembering that the place “took my measure, and I failed.” Mage’s Ruin is where the Red Lady, Endora, first appears in the recovered record; the scene does not establish her as hostile. The Coast, Library of Nuru, Sanctum of the Wise, Shadow Angel Forest, Crustacean Cove, Cathedral, Road, and other named sites expand Gael beyond its principal map labels.

The open record

The builders and chronology of Gael’s ruins, the cathedral’s God of Time, the meaning of its Titan statuary, the full history of the sea temple and Mage’s Ruin, and the exact nature and permanence of the forest’s magic remain incomplete. Soil remediation is a working response to observed damage, not a complete account of every hazard. The durability of settlements and whether restoration can be repeated elsewhere also remain open. The keeper vault preserves additional divine and cosmological questions whose answers should not be visible in the public history.

Hope withers · 27 February 2026

Hope becomes the site of Magnus Niriin's final resurrection and immediate betrayal. After Adelia's Divine Intervention restores him, Magnus accepts a death-working gift from Dumuzi and turns it upon the Tree Shard. Hope begins to wither while Adelia and Jiangshi attempt to preserve her. The event transforms Hope from Gael's emblem of recovery into a wounded participant in its history. Read the complete event.

Recovery at three scales

Gael’s recovery is easiest to understand at three scales. At the environmental scale, Hope, Stake, and Shadowangel Forest prove that life had already begun returning by February 2025. At the civic scale, refugees around the Tower of Gael moved from emergency shelter toward consultation, salvage, and permanent housing. At the regional scale, the Ale-Chemy market and later departure routes show Gael beginning to support commerce and onward travel rather than serving only as a battlefield.

Those scales do not advance evenly. A green place can exist while nearby plains still hold fiends. A market can open while key builders are missing. A trusted traveler may bypass old Void dangers while refugees still lack finished infrastructure. “Restored” is therefore the wrong single label: Gael contains recovery, danger, abandonment, settlement, and exploration at the same time.

A map made from repeated experience

The regional map names monuments, but lived history adds a second geography. Titan’s Watch marks the evidence of Death’s victory. The gas geyser field becomes recognizable after repeated crossings. Crustacean Cove holds the wreck that may become building material. The Tower anchors displaced people. Shadowangel Forest is new enough to demand exploration. The coast becomes the departure point for Verdelune and Larkhollow. Each place gains meaning because later parties inherit earlier observations.

Repeated expeditions have left information that later travelers can use. They have not made the region safe or fully known. They have made some dangers predictable, some routes repeatable, and some civic choices possible. That shared knowledge helps explorers face the region’s risks together.

The region now

Gael is becoming a society while still carrying the consequences of liberation. The Veilguard, the Ale-Chemy Knights, refugees, pilgrims, market workers, academy students, and scattered adventurers do not necessarily share one government or program. Their coexistence is evidence of growth, not proof of political unity.

Major open questions remain public: who completed or abandoned the refugee housing plans, how the newer settlements govern themselves, what caused earlier absences of builders such as Farkur, who is later seen supplying the war again, how safe transport works, and which interior regions remain unexplored. Questions about the oldest nature of Etz Chaim and divine origins remain behind the keeper boundary.

Aid before trade

During the pirate hostage crisis, Fenwick, Brianna and Ithilrune visit a rebuilding coastal refugee settlement on Gael. Edgar, who is organizing fishing and construction, reports eight captives and three pirate ships; those numbers are his account. Fenwick unloads the Knights’ gifts and helps move residents toward the tower for safety. Brianna entertains the children with conjured snow. Edgar asks for building materials, furniture, cooking equipment, healing kits and livestock, and welcomes a proposed Knights outpost. The settlement has about two hundred people by his estimate and no chosen name. The branch establishes delivered aid and a prospective relationship, not a completed outpost, a hostage rescue or an identification with later refugee groups.

Hope beyond a single tree

Hope develops from living ground into a defended sacred presence and a resource for research. In his August 2024 account, Scribonia describes drawing on the Tree to produce a purified, radiant version of a dangerous spell against an undead dragon. That particular demonstration makes Hope an active counterforce; it does not establish that every corruption can be reversed by the same method.

Jiangshi gives the resistance another language. After Nienna’s Hallowing sacrifice, she tells Adelia that love and community can oppose Death: friendship, family and even shared suffering can bind people against isolation. This is her philosophy, not a universal mechanical law.

In December, Jiangshi calls Adelia the true Hope of Gael in her eyes. Adelia answers:

“real hope of this place isn't a tree or a singular person, it's each and every one of us.”
Adelia

The exchange keeps the community beside the person. Adelia’s later transformation deepens her bond with Hope; it does not make every other contribution disappear. Jiangshi and Bitoshi are part of the relational support and later sanctuary work through which that responsibility continues.

The keeping of Gael: choosing the work again

Wrath’s defeat opens a future without securing it forever. Soil work, Stake, the forest, refugee care, housing and exploration continue after the first campaign. Gael’s later history then confronts renewed damage to the very site that made restoration imaginable.

On 27 February 2026, Magnus attacks Hope after Adelia brings him back. The Withering of Hope preserves the witnessed betrayal. Later accounts describe the Tree as dead and turn toward protection and restoration. The meaning of that response is larger than replacing a useful object: people keep choosing the obligations the Tree had come to represent.

Adelia’s later sacrifice and changed existence belong to this continuing history. The exact transformation sequence remains unresolved. Hope’s creation, its wounding, attempts to restore it and Adelia’s transformation are separate stages, rather than one timeless miracle.

Sanctuary and the Place of Recall

In the July 2026 Tower conversation, Jiangshi resets a small sanctuary she and Adelia had made as an escape hatch and casts Word of Recall. Bitoshi helps with the sanctuary area for the Place of Recall. Eldin suggests using the Tree itself as a recall destination, while Jiangshi proposes prayer and meditation spaces linking Hope and Love.

Severina suggests buildings around the Tree; Adelia says building plans will need review. These proposals and the recorded sanctuary work establish care becoming infrastructure. They do not confirm a completed temple, an exact site plan or a permanent settlement charter.

The Veilguard and inherited responsibility

The Veilguard gives the later anti-Death effort an institutional form. Its existing history follows the 2026 leadership selection, the group’s name and the shared obligations tested by Thorn’s loss. In September, Lady Severina Blackveil identifies herself as its leader, guarding the world against Death, and names Pin as a member who helped recover a friend.

Earlier Vanguard testimony preserves Gartina and Scribonia identifying themselves with that company. In July 2026, Severina says collaboration between the Veilguard and Vanguard is the goal. A stated goal does not establish a completed merger, alliance charter or identical membership.

Thorn’s recovery history shows the continuity of Gael’s communal response to loss: grief leads to recovery efforts, pooled resources and promises that persist when rescue fails. Her later presence is established, but the full death-and-return sequence remains incomplete. Neither her story nor Nienna’s makes death consequence-free.

Gael’s enduring achievement is therefore a repeated choice. The first generation makes life possible; later people inherit places, knowledge, losses and unfinished work, and decide to keep rebuilding.

Fenwick’s first-visit guide · March 2025

Fenwick’s guide, preserved in location notes posted on 11–13 March 2025, offers a visitor’s account rather than a complete survey. At the coast he reports no docks for large vessels: ships anchor offshore and travelers transfer by rowboat. He describes wet, difficult stairs and advises carrying less. His suspicion that more infrastructure once stood there remains an inference from what he saw.

Hope as a traveler understood it

In his 12 March account, Fenwick describes a thriving forest offering relief from Gael’s continuing heat and dryness. He worries about fire and gathers stories about the earlier sanctification, Nienna’s statue, Hope, Stake, a Forest Seed and a treant. Those origin stories mix research and hearsay. The recovered restoration scenes above retain priority: living ground and the December 2024 planting already precede Adelia’s later transformation.

A separate scale note estimates Hope at roughly an hour from the Tower and the forest at roughly fifty miles in radius. Fenwick’s own guide instead calls the forest roughly fifty miles wide. The two measures are not equivalent. Their discrepancy remains unresolved, and neither fixes the atlas’s scale.

Titan’s Watch · ruins and interpretation

Fenwick reports ruined Titan statues, a decayed cathedral and a river toward the sea. He reads differences between statues as a possible shift from religious to military leadership. The visible differences are his reported observations; the sequence of rulers and their identities remain his historical theory.

Inside the cathedral’s first chamber, he describes a central wheel, sealed doors, sand altars, red clumps and imagery he reads as draconic and religious. Feeling danger, he observes and withdraws rather than pressing on alone. His impression does not identify the danger’s cause or resolve the cathedral’s builders, worship or mechanisms.

The Plains after Wrath · continuing danger

In the note posted on 13 March, Fenwick reports traveling with Sildithas and Saray and encountering Dream Eaters and a Woe Strider. He says Sildithas required revivification and that he himself was knocked unconscious and nearly died. These are his expedition recollections, not a newly verified casualty chronology or proof that every later recollection describes this same encounter.

He sees an opportunity to harvest components but interprets the new creatures as nature rebalancing after Wrath’s forces were cleared. That ecological explanation, and any suggestion that his party was first to explore afterward, remain his conclusions. Liberation did not make his journey safe.

Read the campaign across its people

Gael · the war and the keeping follows the choices, changing knowledge and consequences across this regional history. The unresolved record preserves the transitions still needing evidence.

The August intervention before the Hallowing

The early living foothold, the freeing of Hope and the Hallowing are distinct stages. The Hope description is posted on 2 August 2024; the subsequent quest identifies the tree with Adelia and Elenia’s earlier miracle. On 5–6 August, the company finds it being drained by a shadow. Adelia severs that attachment after Daylight and Dispel Magic fail to release it, and a transformed luminous tree remains after the damaging blast.

September’s Hallowing is later work, sustained through danger and ending in an eruption of life. Nienna’s sacrifice and the exhaustion of Adelia, Gartina and Elenia belong to that later sequence. The earlier intervention does not replace those contributions or date the very first casting precisely.

December’s soil work, Stake and forest growth form another stage again. Akarian’s January observation of trees and life supplies a later witness to the changed landscape, even as he says it still feels like death to him. That corroborates continued presence, without explaining the forest’s lasting mechanism.

The library as inherited work

The Library of Nuru keeps spell copying, incomplete research and mutual preparation within the Tower. Fenwick and Scribonia share access to spells, Minerva offers expedition help, and Fenwick later joins the Veilguard there without leaving the Ale-Chemy Knights. Study and agreements between companions continue alongside the work of restoring the land.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4.

The Plains remain a place to learn and retreat

Repeated hunts from the Tower bring Severina and Ryvyt together with Tobias, Minerva, Nex and Fenwick in different companies. They prepare elixirs, discuss when to retreat, fight and gather. Butterflies, dragons, strange predators and disorienting fog remain hazards after Wrath’s fall. Severina’s jokes that dragons fear them are not evidence that the region has been cleared.

When Minerva doubts her performance, Severina points to what she survived and contributed rather than accepting her verdict of incompetence. In a later outing Fenwick’s psychic attack makes a predator easier for the others to hit; the narrator presents his explanation as an inference about its reflexes. The group defeats it and a fiery bird before discussing a return. Roads and a future town remain planning work, not new map features.

gallery.alt: Shadow Angel Forest — orb found along the stream
gallery.caption: Gael. Anky follows a shallow stream and spots an orb, then crouches for cover. The image illustrates that forest encounter; it does not independently establish a named portal or another world.

gallery.title: Shadow Angel Forest — hole found during the hunt
gallery.alt: Shadow Angel Forest — hole found during the hunt
gallery.caption: Gael. Qualified reference. Player-directed hunt narration calls for finding a hole in the ground after a successful Survival roll. The image illustrates that descent scene, without establishing a separate named site or exact dimensions.

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — opening landscape reference
gallery.alt: Plains of Trial — opening landscape reference
gallery.caption: Gael. The opening description identifies enemy territory on Gael. The image supplies a landscape reference without a measured route or separately identified landmark.

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — smoke-covered interior
gallery.caption: Gael. The narrator describes the party wandering deeper into the land under smog and toxic clouds. The attachment illustrates that journey, not all of present-day Gael.

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — burning fissure in the hills
gallery.alt: Plains of Trial — burning fissure in the hills

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — cavern seen by Elenia

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — beyond the last border

gallery.title: Plains of Trial — bleak day beneath the smog
gallery.alt: Plains of Trial — bleak day beneath the smog
gallery.caption: Gael. The narrator explicitly describes an unusually dark day even for Gael, with smog blanketing the air. Preserve the scene’s weather and posting context.

gallery.title: Gael hunt — sunlit woodland reference
